reasons: The cap rewrite fully lands the preferred greater-of construct: lowercase fee basis across the whole Agreement, 12 months preceding the claim, and the USD 1,000,000 limb, curing the illusory USD 12,000 first-Order-Form cap.

Mutuality, the consequential-damages exclusion and all preferred carve-outs (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP) are present and untouched.

The preferred level is incomplete on one atomic element: 21.3 says only that "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees for conforming Services is not damages", which is narrower than "Customer's payment obligations are not damages" — and "Fees" is defined as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee, so the carve-out barely bites. Suggested minimal fix: replace "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" with "amounts due under this Agreement".

Minimality holds: one targeted operator/basis replacement in 21.1, no fallback-only terms imported, no new exceptions, no boilerplate, and untouched sentences (21.2 direct-damages list, 21.3 definition) remain effective with no dangling references.
